justification: New nightly alarm: re-serves 28 real addresses from production and goes red when one address's answer widens, shrinks, gains a council or chapter it never had, serves a precinct rule with no precinct key, or comes back empty with no stated reason. On 2026-10-15 every address was being served 800-2,750 rules and no check noticed, because every check counts database rows. Read-only against a public endpoint; no source file of the product is touched.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: Mutations measured 2026-10-18: judge() returning [] always -> 7 failed / 4 passed; the precinct-key test disabled in shape() -> 1 failed / 10 passed; clean -> 11 passed. Live: exit 1 when any panel address moves outside its box (first baseline run went red on 019 Seaforth, 0 rules, until its reason was recorded).
falsifiable_check.external_authority: Production /api/provisions/for-property, called with the exact query the assessment page sent for each address in the 2026-10-16 audit (run 8). The baseline is that endpoint's own answer, accepted with a written reason.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: First baseline run 2026-10-18 went red on 019 9 Benelong St Seaforth: 'served 0 rules -- an empty answer with no stated reason', exit 1. Unreachable production (--base-url http://127.0.0.1:9): 'UNKNOWN -- 28/28 unreachable', exit 2.

pre_impl.existing_data: DQ-143/144/146 (scripts/dq_probe_live.py) count known wrong-area defect classes in the database; check_served_answer_quality.py scores rows through conveyancing_db; check_served_output.py asserts HTTP contracts and is wired into no workflow; build_packets.py samples 10 rules per address for a person and keeps no baseline. The panel and its queries come from build_packets run 8.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed a ceiling on rules per address would separate bad addresses from good ones. Measured: every address receives 96-99% of its council's 'generic' layer by design (Parramatta 2,111-2,179 of 2,195), and the cleanest audited address (Winston Hills) is served 1,995. A count ceiling would be red everywhere and invented, so the alarm detects CHANGE plus three plainly-broken shapes, and says it cannot judge today's level (that is DQ-143/144).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One script, one committed panel, one test file, one data-watch step added to the existing issue logic. No new tracker: a red run raises the existing data-watch issue.

functions.name: judge
functions.input: a panel entry (baseline, optional expected_empty) and today's shape()
functions.output: list of reasons the address is outside its box; empty = inside
functions.if_none: a missing baseline is itself a reason (red), never a pass

values.read_at: run 8 (2026-10-16 23:04) vs production 2026-10-18 on the same 28 queries: largest movement +2.4% (008 Haberfield, 1,971 -> 2,018) and -3.3% (018 Northern Beaches, 637 -> 616)
values.if_missing: change-detection tolerances, not regulatory values; set at three times observed drift

values.value: first live check after baseline: 28/28 inside, exit 0
values.if_missing: without it the alarm could be red on day one from noise

break_it.scenario: Today's baseline already contains wrong-area rules (16 per 100 in the 2026-10-15 audit), so the alarm accepts them.
break_it.what_happens: It stays green on a known-wrong answer.
break_it.how: Stated in the docstring and the baseline reason: green means no worse than accepted, never correct. DQ-143/144 measure the level; when they clear rules, the shrink shows here and the rebaseline reason records why.

break_it.scenario: Production is down or slow at 20:00 UTC.
break_it.what_happens: Addresses are reported as could-not-measure; above a fifth of the panel the run exits 2, which fails the step.
break_it.how: UNKNOWN is never a pass; below the fifth the unmeasured count is printed.

break_it.scenario: Frozen queries go stale when the Planning Portal changes a property's facts.
break_it.what_happens: The alarm keeps testing the old query; it does not see geocoder or /api/property changes.
break_it.how: Deliberate: frozen inputs make a change attributable to the route or the data. /api/property is out of scope here.

residual_risk: Detects change, not correctness. Panel is 28 addresses in 13 councils; councils outside the panel are not watched.

post_merge.db_reset: No - read-only; calls the public for-property endpoint, writes nothing to the database.
post_merge.secrets: No - the data-watch step needs no secret.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after merge, run data-watch by workflow_dispatch once and confirm the 'Rules per address' step prints PASSED -- 28 addresses.
